title: The new `suspended` prop is covered only at the ConfigScreen integration level.…
description:
The new `suspended` prop is covered only at the ConfigScreen integration level. Consider a direct TabBar unit test asserting Left/Right fires when suspended=false and stands down when suspended=true, to pin the presentational contract independently of its one caller.

Source: cam/issue-316
Review round: 1

suggestion-fingerprint: ef4fb66752be

spec.scope: Add a direct TabBar unit test that pins the `suspended` prop's Left/Right navigation contract independently of its single ConfigScreen caller. Currently the `suspended` behavior is only exercised transitively at the ConfigScreen integration level (the fieldFocus===3/4 notify sub-branches). This story adds a focused unit test rendering TabBar directly.
acceptanceCriteria: A new test renders TabBar directly (not via ConfigScreen) with suspended={false} and asserts Left and Right key events fire tab navigation (the active index changes / onChange is invoked).
The same test file asserts that with suspended={true}, Left and Right key events are suppressed and do NOT change the active tab / do NOT invoke navigation.
The test lives alongside the existing UI tests and follows the established ink-testing-library render() style already used in the suite.
typecheck passes and the full test suite is green with the new test added (net new passing test, zero failures).
gotchas: The `suspended` prop was introduced for CAM-316 and is presently covered only at the ConfigScreen integration level; the point of this story is a direct presentational unit test, so drive TabBar in isolation.
Use ink-testing-library render() + stdin.write for Left/Right arrow escape sequences, mirroring the existing config-screen test patterns; do not add a new test harness.
Test-only change: do not modify TabBar source unless a genuine test-seam gap forces it (surface rather than refactor).
